thread: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request
subject: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request — Council-held planning, heritage and public-authority record for Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr, Llandough
body:
Democratic and Scrutiny Services
Vale of Glamorgan Council
Democratic@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

cc: FoiUnit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk (for information only — this is not a new FOI request)

Dear Democratic and Scrutiny Services,

Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / request for a focused Task and Finish Review

I am a resident with a long-standing family connection to Great House Farm (Tÿ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth. A public documentary archive of the site is maintained at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

I request that the Council consider a focused Scrutiny Topic Suggestion leading to a Task and Finish Review (or other appropriate scrutiny mechanism) concerning the Council-held planning, heritage, environmental and public-authority record relating to Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr / Church View Close.

Proposed scope (within the Council’s remit):

• the Council-held planning, heritage, environmental and public-authority record relating to Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr / Church View Close;
• the chronology of Council decisions, records and responses from the mid-twentieth century onwards;
• identification of missing, contradictory or unresolved Council-held records and, where appropriate, referral to the body with the relevant jurisdiction;
• consideration of the site’s heritage and historical record, including its proposed interpretation in the Tÿ Mawr replica museum project in Puerto Madryn, Chubut; and
• recommendations within the Council’s powers, without asking the Council to determine private title, criminal liability or matters reserved to courts or other public bodies.

This is an evidence-review and accountability route. It is not a request for the Council to decide private title or liability.

I am happy to complete the online Scrutiny Topic Suggestion Form if preferred, or to supply any further information the Democratic Services team requires.

Please acknowledge receipt and indicate the process and timescale for consideration.

Kind regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request
subject: RE: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request — Council-held planning, heritage and public-authority record for Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr, Llandough
body:
Dear Mr Buckler,

Many thanks for your e-mail below and your request for Scrutiny to consider the topic suggested as part of it's Task and Finish work.

Unfortunately, on this occasion we will be unable to consider the request for several reasons:

1. The purpose of Task and Finish is to review existing policy Council considerations and identify areas for future policy direction at a strategic level impacting on a county wide basis. These topics are purposefully strategic in manner, and are based upon areas that Committees determine to have the most positive impact.

2. In addition to the above, the purpose of Scrutiny is not to review evidence related to individual historical decisions and make subsequent recommendations, particularly related to planning, which should be navigated through other channels.

3. We are aware through other correspondence to which you have copied us into that there are ongoing concerns being raised through a variety of channels including Welsh Government, CADW, MSs and MPs, and as such it would not be appropriate for a Scrutiny Task and Finish to add an additional layer of stakeholders and complexity in exploring the issues; notwithstanding points 1 and 2 raised.

Kind Regards,
James

thread: FOI/EIR 00211557 — s.52/land charges, planning register, condition 16–18 chain, 92/00671/RES; missing appendices C, D and E
subject: FOI/EIR 00211557 and earlier requests – formal chase of three missing planning appendices (C, D and E)
body:
Dear FOI Team,

I refer to the partial disclosures already made and to the still-open requests concerning Great House Farm / Tý Mawr / Church View Close (including 00210772, 00211463, 00211483, 00211484 and 00211557).

The planning report’s Appendices C, D and E remain missing. These form part of the public planning record for the site and are required for the completeness of the evidence library. Please:

2. Either disclose them in full or state the precise exemption relied upon for each.

thread: EIR 00210772 — internal review and formal chases
subject: [1] RE: Great House Farm, Llandough – Request 00210772 – Internal Review – Formal Chase
body:
Information Governance Team,

*Case Ref 00210772 — internal review requested 7 July 2026*

Thank you for your email of 11 September. You said that you would try to
update me by the end of the following week with a clearer timeframe. I have
not received that update.

Under regulation 11(4) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004,
an internal review should be completed as soon as possible and no later
than 40 working days after receipt of the request for reconsideration. On
my calculation, that period expired on 2 September 2026. The review is
therefore now overdue.

I appreciate that further historical documentation has been located and
that you may need to consult third parties. I am not asking you to
compromise any proper consultation process. However, I ask that you now
provide the following by *Tuesday 6 October 2026*:

1. *A firm date* by which the completed internal review decision will be
issued.

2. *A non-disclosive description of the further documentation located*,
including, so far as presently known:
- its approximate date or date range;
- who created or supplied it;
- how it came into the Council's possession; and
- approximately how many documents are involved.

I am asking for a description of the material and its provenance, rather
than disclosure of its substantive contents.

3. *Confirmation that the newly located documentation is being preserved in
its present form*, without alteration, destruction or disposal, while
the internal review and any subsequent complaint to the Information
Commissioner remain outstanding.

4. *Release now of any material that can properly be disclosed without
awaiting third-party consultation*, where the Council has already
established that no exemption or other restriction prevents disclosure.

If I do not receive a substantive response by *6 October 2026*, I will
refer the continuing delay to the Information Commissioner's Office without
further notice.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: EIR 00210772 — internal review and formal chases
subject: Re: Great House Farm, Llandough – Request 00210772 – Internal Review – Formal Chase – unanswered points from 30 September and 11 September
body:
Information Governance Team
cc: Monitoring Officer; Data Protection Officer

Case Ref 00210772 — Internal Review requested 7 July 2026

This is a formal chase of unanswered points already put to you. It is not a new request and must not be used to restart any clock.

On 11 September 2026 you wrote that service areas had found further historical documentation, that you were still sifting it, and that because some of it is “not necessarily Council documentation but is nonetheless in the Council’s possession” you were considering whether to consult third parties. You said you would try to give a clearer timetable by the end of the following week (i.e. by 18 September 2026).

On 30 September 2026 I asked, by Tuesday 6 October 2026, for:
1. A firm date by which the completed internal review decision will be issued;
2. A non-disclosive description of the further documentation located (date range, creator/supplier, how it came into the Council’s possession, approximate volume);
3. Confirmation that the newly located documentation is being preserved without alteration, destruction or disposal; and
4. Immediate release of any material that can properly be disclosed without awaiting third-party consultation.

None of those four points has been answered.

What you have not said
You have not identified a single document found in the September sift. You have not named any third-party consultee class, the date any consultation was sent, or the date by which a reply was required. You have not stated whether the material is held under EIR or FOIA. You have not addressed the child / personal-data point previously raised. You have not confirmed a preservation hold. Silence on each of these points is itself a recorded position.

What is now required (unchanged from the unanswered requests)
(a) Issue the internal review decision. On any view the ICO’s recommended maximum of 40 working days from the request for review (7 July 2026) has long passed. If you contend that EIR does not apply, say so expressly and identify the statutory basis for treating the request under FOIA alone.

(b) Attach a schedule of every document found in the further search: date, description, format, holding service, whether Council or third-party record in the Council’s possession, and the decision on each (disclose / part-disclose / withhold with the precise regulation or section).

(c) If any third-party consultation has occurred or is proposed, name the class of consultee, the date the consultation was sent, and the deadline set for reply. A consultee’s silence is not a ground to withhold.

(d) Confirm in writing that every document in the sift, and every related planning, enforcement, legal, committee, land, finance and correspondence record (including predecessor-authority material), is under a formal preservation hold and will not be destroyed, weeded, transferred or disposed of while 00210772 and related requests remain open.

(e) Address the child / personal-data point: if any record has been withheld or is being considered for withholding because it mentions a child, identify the record and the exemption. If no such withholding exists, say so expressly. Treat the personal-data element also as a subject-access request under UK GDPR for Sion Hywel Buckler (child occupant in 1988).

The 7 July 2026 answer treated the matter as a planning-register query. That was too narrow. The sift must cover the full list previously set out (planning files including unpublished appendices, enforcement, building control, environmental health, demolition, legal-services files, member/officer correspondence, land/estates files, finance records, and predecessor-authority transfers to Glamorgan Archives).

Public-accountability questions (to be answered from the documents, including those found in September)
1. Was any Council or predecessor expenditure, fee, cost, grant or works associated with the occupation, demolition or redevelopment?
2. Was any Council or predecessor land, right, permission or undertaking involved?
3. Were officers or members told of anything that contradicted or qualified the ownership, occupation, heritage or demolition account then being used?
4. What accounting, audit, legal, planning, committee and correspondence records survive?
5. Was any irregularity, conflict, material error or control failure identified, reported, or formally accounted for?
6. If the Council’s position is that there is nothing to examine, state that expressly and identify the documents relied on.

By return
Within 5 working days: the document schedule, the preservation confirmation, and either the child-exemption notice or a clear statement that none exists.
Within 10 working days: the internal review decision with copies of everything you are able to disclose.

This email records that the four points put to you on 30 September 2026 remain unanswered as of 6 October 2026. If no substantive response is received, the continuing failure to complete the internal review will be referred to the Information Commissioner without further notice.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
